key_insight: Annotator-specific free-text explanations contain subtle but stable signals, and LLMs can be trained to reproduce individual annotator label+explanation behavior by optimizing across annotator preferences.
problem_solved: The paper addresses how to model and reproduce human label variation beyond discrete label disagreement — specifically, recovering annotator-specific reasoning/preferences (free-text explanations) rather than collapsing to a majority view or ignoring individual annotator behavior.
method: Collect sentence-pair data (NLI and paraphrase judgment) with four annotators per instance, including free-text explanations.
Analyze per-annotator stability to quantify how consistent individual explanation patterns are.

Train LLMs with cross-annotator preference optimization: a preference-based objective that aligns model outputs (label + explanation) with annotator-specific choices to produce personalized explanations.
impact: Enables models that reflect individual annotator reasoning, improving interpretability, dataset modeling, and personalization; useful for better label-conditioning, debiasing, and downstream evaluation when human disagreement encodes meaningful preferences.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: data (annotators + explanations) → cross-annotator preference optimization → annotator-specific model outputs
Per-annotator similarity heatmap or clustering showing how explanations group by annotator
Side-by-side examples: same input with different annotator explanations and corresponding model-generated explanations
Bar chart comparing model fidelity to each annotator (reproduction accuracy / explanation similarity)
paper_title: Human Label Variation as Stable Signal: Learning Annotator-Specific Explanation Behavior via Cross-Annotator Preference Optimization
paper_authors: Beiduo Chen, Pingjun Hong, Ziyun Zhang, Benjamin Roth, Anna Korhonen
